newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom to soft-launch VOD in July.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom to soft-launch VOD in July.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Sunday it had signed a supply agreement with a joint venture of two local film distributors and would soft-launch its video-on-demand (VOD) services in July.
"We will have a soft launch of VOD services in July before a full-scale commercial launch in October," William Lo, managing director of the company's IMS unit, told reporters.

Lo said the firm had signed an exclusive film agency and supply agreement with a venture formed by Golden Harvest Entertainment Co Ltd and China Star Entertainment Ltd to provide Cantonese-language movies to the VOD service.

"We have prepared to invest more than HK$300 million in the content acquisition for our VOD services, such as purchasing films and television programmes, and Cantonese movies will be the major part of the acquisition," Lo said.
He declined to disclose the value of the five-year agreement with the joint venture.
Golden Harvest and China Star will provide their own "top quality" films as well as sourcing other local films for Hong Kong Telecom's VOD service, a Golden Harvest spokesman said.
Hong Kong Telecom has said it plans to invest more than HK$10 billion over 10 years in interactive television services, which comprise VOD, home shopping and home banking.
"Looking at interactive services as a whole, we are looking at a breakeven at the fourth year," Lo said.
Lo said the company said it expects to have 3,000 VOD customers in the first three months after the soft launch at eight private housing estates.
"From October onward, the full-scale VOD services will be in place and our target is between 25,000 and 28,000 customers in the first two years," he added.
The company said VOD would be available to about 15 percent of Hong Kong's 1.6 million households in October and to about 80 percent by mid-1999.
Home banking services would be available in January 1998, Lo said.
